Handbreadth
HAND-bredth
noun
Hebrew tophach / tephach, the width of the hand at the base of the fingers, about three inches; the smallest standard measure of length.

📖 Biblical Definition

The handbreadth was the smallest standard measure of length in ancient Israel, the width of the four fingers at the base of the hand, about three inches, and it serves in Scripture both as a literal measure and as a vivid figure of the brevity of human life. As a measure it fixes dimensions in the tabernacle and temple: the border of an handbreadth around the table of shewbread, the brim of the molten sea an handbreadth thick. As a figure it gives one of the most piercing words on the shortness of our days: Behold, thou hast made my days as an handbreadth, and mine age is as nothing before thee; verily every man at his best state is altogether vanity. The psalmist measures the whole span of a life against the eternity of God and finds it no longer than the width of a hand—here and gone, a vapor, a shadow that declineth. The dictionary records the handbreadth as a unit of biblical measure and treasures its great spiritual use: to teach the soul to number its days. Set beside the everlasting God, the longest life is but a handbreadth; and the lesson of the measure is the prayer of Moses—so teach us to number our days, that we may apply our hearts unto wisdom—that the brevity of life might drive the believer to lay hold on the eternal.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The smallest measure of length, the width of the hand (about three inches); a literal temple measure and a piercing figure of the brevity of life—our days made as a handbreadth.

HANDBREADTH, the width of the hand, about three inches; the smallest standard length.

A literal measure in the tabernacle and temple furnishings.

The border of the table of shewbread an handbreadth round about (Exo 25:25).

A figure of the brevity of life: my days as an handbreadth (Psa 39:5).

Teaches the soul to number its days against the eternity of God.

📖 Key Scripture

Psa 39:5 — "Behold, thou hast made my days as an handbreadth; and mine age is as nothing before thee: verily every man at his best state is altogether vanity. Selah."

Exo 25:25 — "And thou shalt make unto it a border of an hand breadth round about, and thou shalt make a golden crown to the border thereof round about."

1Ki 7:26 — "And it was an hand breadth thick, and the brim thereof was wrought like the brim of a cup, with flowers of lilies: it contained two thousand baths."

2Ch 4:5 — "And the thickness of it was an handbreadth, and the brim of it like the work of the brim of a cup, with flowers of lilies; and it received and held three thousand baths."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition, though the age that hides death and dreams of indefinite life forgets the lesson of the handbreadth: that our days are short and must be numbered.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The lesson the measure presses is one the present age labors to forget: the brevity of human life. The handbreadth is about three inches; the psalmist makes the whole span of a man as an handbreadth, his age as nothing before God, every man at his best state altogether vanity. The modern world hides death behind hospital walls, distracts the soul with endless amusement, and dreams of indefinitely extended life; and so it forgets to number its days. To live as though life were long is to be a fool with a vapor’s span, building bigger barns while the soul is required.

The principle to recover is the numbering of our short days unto wisdom. The handbreadth measures the longest life against the eternity of God and finds it a hand’s width—here and gone, a shadow that declineth. This is no counsel of despair but of wisdom: so teach us to number our days, prayed Moses, that we may apply our hearts unto wisdom. The believer who reckons his days a handbreadth lays hold the more firmly on the eternal, redeeming the time, setting his affection on things above, and laboring for the life that does not pass away.
